method: Quick triage from each molecule's chemistry and common handling guidance; not measured on these plates.
sources: Kozikowski et al. 2003, J Biomol Screen 8:205 and 8:210
Cheng et al. 2003, J Biomol Screen 8:292

17-AAG KOS953.why: Benzoquinone ansamycin: the quinone is redox-labile and light-sensitive.

Abiraterone.why: Stable steroid scaffold (the free drug, not the acetate prodrug).

Amlodipine Besylate.why: Dihydropyridine: light-sensitive, though slower than nifedipine.

Aripiprazole.why: Stable; at most mild light sensitivity.

Aspirin Acetylsalicylic acid.why: The acetyl ester hydrolyses to salicylic acid as DMSO takes up water.

Atorvastatin Calcium.why: Hydroxy acid can lactonise and oxidise in solution.

Axitinib.why: Styryl double bond isomerises in light; poorly soluble, can fall out on thaw.

Budesonide.why: Corticosteroid side chain oxidises slowly in solution.

Carfilzomib PR-171.why: Peptide epoxyketone: the epoxide warhead opens with water; made up fresh.

Clopidogrel.why: Methyl ester hydrolyses and the thiophene oxidises in solution.

Colchicine.why: Light turns it into inactive lumicolchicines.

Curcumin.why: Degrades quickly in solution by autoxidation; light-sensitive.

Cyclosporin A.why: Robust cyclic peptide (can stick to plastic, which is not decay).

DAPT GSI-IX.why: Dipeptide tert-butyl ester: slow hydrolysis in wet DMSO.

Diltiazem HCl.why: Acetyl ester hydrolyses to the weaker desacetyl-diltiazem.

Enalapril.why: Ethyl-ester prodrug: hydrolyses and cyclises (diketopiperazine) in solution.

Epothilone B.why: Epoxide macrolactone: sensitive to acid, water and heat.

Everolimus RAD001.why: Triene macrolide that oxidises in solution; supplied with antioxidant.

Famotidine.why: Stable in DMSO; hydrolyses only slowly in water.

Ganetespib STA-9090.why: Resorcinol triazolone; reasonably stable in DMSO.

Isoprenaline HCl.why: Catecholamine: oxidises quickly in solution (turns pink, then brown).

Leflunomide.why: Isoxazole ring opens to teriflunomide with water and base.

Lovastatin.why: Lactone prodrug hydrolyses to its hydroxy acid.

MLN2238 Ixazomib.why: Boronic acid: oxidative deboronation in solution; made up fresh.

Mercaptopurine 6-MP.why: Thiol oxidises to disulfides in solution.

Nifedipine.why: Dihydropyridine that degrades within hours in light.

Orlistat.why: The beta-lactone warhead hydrolyses with water.

Paclitaxel Taxol.why: Ester-rich taxane: epimerises and hydrolyses; can fall out on thaw.

Panobinostat.why: Hydroxamic acid: slow hydrolysis in wet DMSO.

Pimecrolimus.why: Macrolactam like tacrolimus; slow degradation in solution.

Pravastatin sodium.why: Hydroxy acid lactonises and isomerises, fastest in acid.

Quercetin.why: Polyphenol that autoxidises in DMSO and in light.

Ramipril.why: Ester prodrug: hydrolyses and cyclises (diketopiperazine) in solution.

Rapamycin Sirolimus.why: Macrolide that degrades in solution (ring opening, oxidation), faster warm.

Resveratrol.why: Light turns trans- into weaker cis-resveratrol; oxidises.

Romidepsin FK228.why: Disulfide prodrug: sensitive to reducing conditions.

Simvastatin Zocor.why: Lactone prodrug hydrolyses to its hydroxy acid.

Sorafenib.why: Stable urea; poorly soluble in water but fine in DMSO.

Tacrolimus FK506.why: Macrolide: epimerises and degrades slowly in solution.

Vinblastine sulfate.why: Vinca alkaloid: sensitive to light and oxidation; kept cold.

Vorinostat SAHA.why: Hydroxamic acid: slow hydrolysis in wet DMSO.
